faq.question: What can I do if my health insurance claim is rejected?
faq.answer: Write to the insurer's grievance officer with the rejection letter, the policy clause and your reasons. If they don't resolve it within about 15 days, register it on IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal, then take it to the Insurance Ombudsman, which is free for claims up to ₹50 lakh.

faq.question: Can an insurer reject a claim for non-disclosure after five years?
faq.answer: No, except for established fraud. IRDAI's rules say that after 60 months of continuous coverage, a health policy or claim can't be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation. Time on ported or migrated policies counts toward the 60 months.

faq.question: How long do I have to complain to the Insurance Ombudsman?
faq.answer: One year from the date the insurer rejected your complaint, or from the end of the one-month period if the insurer didn't reply. You must complain to the insurer first.

faq.question: Does the Insurance Ombudsman charge a fee?
faq.answer: No. There's no fee to file, you don't need a lawyer, and hearings can be held online. The ombudsman handles claims up to ₹50 lakh and must pass an award within three months of receiving all the requirements.

faq.question: Is a cashless denial the same as a claim rejection?
faq.answer: No. If cashless is refused, you can pay the hospital and claim reimbursement, and the insurer decides again on the full documents. Insurers must decide cashless requests within one hour under IRDAI's rules.
